newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat drops to new lows on conditions, supply.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat drops to new lows on conditions, supply.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed sharply lower and new contract lows were set in all but the nearby December contract.
An impressive rating for the 1997 U.S. winter wheat crop, building supplies of wheat worldwide, and falling prices all combined to drive the market lower, traders said.

"It feels like total liquidation in here. First off the conditions were negative (bearish), Argentina is offering wheat at $124.00 (per tonne) and the EC is trying to get rid of wheat," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for Chicago-based trade house FIMAT Futures.

USDA Monday said 75 pct of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in good to excellent shape as of Sunday, up from 56 pct in that category a year ago. USDA also said 93 pct of the U.S. crop had been seeded as of Sunday, a hefty seedings level.
The new contract low for March wheat is $3.63-1/2 per bushel, down from the previous low of $3.65-1/2 set Friday.
Fund selling led the way down with Rosenthal Collins and Dean Witter Reynolds each a featured seller of two million bushels of December, the traders said.
Wheat closed five to 11 cents per bushel lower, with December down 11 at $3.68-3/4.

Technical indicators remain bearish with the key moving averages pointing to further losses. The market is short term oversold with the nine day relative strength index (RSI) on a daily basis for the December closing at 25.6 points. The market views an RSI of 30 or less as indicative of an oversold market.
December closed below first support at $3.74-3/4 and just above the second support level of $3.66-1/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 19,000, up from 17,046 Monday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Prudential Securities sold 450 July $3.30 puts at 14 cents and Smith Barney sold 300 March $3.80 calls at 10-1/2 cents, traders said.
Volatility for December closed at 19 percent and March 18 percent.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000, up from 7,354 Monday.
